(a) stage-1 had only two status assignments, both in OrderService: PlaceOrderAsync initializer `Status = "new"` (:16) and CancelOrderAsync `order.Status = "cancelled"` (:34) — not 'several scripts', and no paid/ship change existed. 'Every status change Đơn Hàng allows' holds only for the application code.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Reading `Order` alone now tells you every status change the application's code can make, named in business words: mark paid, ship, cancel. At stage-1 the assignments sat as plain lines inside `OrderService`'s methods, with no check of the status they started from.

issues.text: Overstated. At stage-1 there were only two status assignments, both in OrderService (PlaceOrderAsync `Status = "new"`, CancelOrderAsync `order.Status = "cancelled"`); 'several scripts' inflates this. 'Every status change Đơn Hàng allows' ignores that stage-2 repo scripts (scripts/backend/staff-only.sh:11 and others) set orders.status by SQL, bypassing Order. issues.text: Line 57 is `Status = "";` in the private constructor, which Entities.cs:51-54 says exists 'For EF Core only' and whose values EF Core overwrites from the loaded row. It does not give an order its starting status; only line 69 (public constructor, `"new"`) does.
issues.quote: Lines 57 and 69 are in the two constructors, which give an order its starting status and are the topic of later lessons.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Line 69 is in the public constructor, which gives every new order the status `new`; line 57 is in a private constructor kept for EF Core. Both are the topic of later lessons."

issues.quote: Run `git grep -n "Status = \"" -- "DonHang.Domain/*.cs"` to list every line in `DonHang.Domain` that assigns an order status.
issues.fix: Add "in a bash shell (Git Bash on Windows)" to step 1, or use single quotes around the pattern: `git grep -n 'Status = "' -- 'DonHang.Domain/*.cs'`.
